Checking whether the uncommitted files in this checkout already match the knot, which would make a pull safe.

Right now Slab shows one rock for this session. That's megazo, on ttys001. The other rock, besulu, belongs to the Codex window next to it. The ledger has one marker for each session. Every Claude hook skips when `AESEL_SESSION_ID` is set, and that variable is set inside Aesel's inner Claude, so the inner process can't make a rock of its own. Only one prox server is running. So I couldn't reproduce the second rock. It may have come from your first prompt here, which failed twice with "OAuth session expired" before the session restarted. Or it may have come from the old Loopboy behaviour: the knot's latest commit, 2f4c929734, makes Loopboy a mode of an existing prox instead of a separate one. If you see two again, tell me while it's on screen and I'll capture it. I did find one small bug. `aesel/src/slab-session.mjs:118` hardcodes `provider_agent_type: "codex"`, so this Claude-backed session is labeled codex in the ledger. Nothing reads that field yet.

On "fully updated", partly. Your installed `a` is a symlink into this checkout, so it runs whatever the checkout has. It reports 0.8.20, the same as the served version. But local `main` is 82 commits behind the knot. The Aesel and most Slab files are uncommitted edits that are byte-identical to the knot's versions. Three files are being edited right now and differ from the knot: `apple/whistlegraph/README.md`, `AppDelegate.swift` and `MenuBuilder.swift`. That's probably the Codex session next door. I didn't pull, so I wouldn't pull out from under it. Production also hasn't caught up. The served tarball predates the knot's "Release Aesel on its own" commit, so `ac-deploy aesel` hasn't run since then.

On speed, I ran `aesel/bin/bench-tui.py` against a loopback stream, with no model calls. Aesel opens in about 110 ms, against 350 ms for bare Claude. First reply takes 260 ms with the Codex backend and 500 ms with the Claude backend, against 800 ms for bare Claude. Aesel's own startup takes about 90 ms, and half of that is importing `tui.mjs`. The real cost is the `claude` CLI itself. Spawning it takes about 1.8 s before it's ready, whether it loads the 38 MCP servers or none. Aesel already hides that by connecting before you type.

The biggest win left is per turn, not at startup. Aesel doesn't pass `--strict-mcp-config`, so the inner Claude loads all 38 project and user MCP servers. Their tool names go into the context on every turn. Limiting the inner Claude to just `ac` and `easel-media` would make turns lighter and faster. You would lose prox, frame and the rest inside Aesel, which I've been using in this answer. A middle path is a short allowlist for pro sessions. Tell me which you want and I'll make the change.

Backend can switch mid-session, so the right place is `connected()`, which already stamps the provider session id. Finding its callers.
`backend` is already reassigned before every call, so each site can pass `backend.id`. Making the edits.
The slab-session test passes with the new assertion. Running the rest of Aesel's unit tests.

The rock now records which engine is answering. Before, `provider_agent_type` was hardcoded to `"codex"` in `aesel/src/slab-session.mjs`. Now it starts empty and `connected()` stamps it with the backend's id: claude, codex, ac or open. All three places in `tui.mjs` that call `connected()` pass `backend.id`, including the two that run after a `/backend` swap, so the label follows a mid-session switch.

I added an assertion for the field to `test/slab-session.test.mjs`. The full Aesel unit suite passes: 548 of 557 tests passed, none failed, and the 9 not counted as passes were skipped or todo.

This window is still running the old code, so its rock keeps saying codex until Aesel restarts. I haven't committed anything. Local `main` is 82 commits behind the knot, and the Codex session next door has uncommitted work in the same tree. Tell me when to commit and I'll stage only these three files.
